english.title: Unlawfully disclose information for an industrial training board
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed information in contravention of section 6(2) of the Industrial Training Act 1982 in that **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6(6)(c) of the Industrial Training Act 1982.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
disclose information in contravention of s. 6(2)

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 6(1) provides that anindustrial training board may require employers in the industry to furnish suchreturns and other information of a kind approved by the Secretary of State andto keep such records of a kind approved by him and produce them for examinationon behalf of the board as appear to the board to be necessary for carrying outits functions.
(ii) Section 6(8) provides that where an offence under this section committed by a body corporateis proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to beattributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary orother similar officer of the body corporate, or any person who was purportingto act in any such capacity, he, as well as the body corporate, shall be guiltyof that offence and be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the prescribed sum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
